Tunnicliff TAKEAWAYS Net Sales -- $2.3869 billion, an increase of 14.7% year over year driven by share gains with larger customers and broad-based demand across core end markets. Daily Sales Rate -- $37.3 million, growing 14.7% year over year and reflecting the company's continued market outperformance despite a stable industrial backdrop. Gross Profit Margin -- 44.6%, a decrease of 75 basis points year over year due to a 40 basis-point headwind from net price/cost and customer mix shifts toward larger accounts. Operating Income -- $501.8 million, representing a 21.0% margin that remained consistent year over year as SG&A leverage fully offset gross margin contraction. Diluted Net Income Per Share -- $0.33, an increase of 15.9% compared to $0.29 in the second quarter of 2025. Digital Footprint Sales -- $1.4929 billion, representing 61.6% of total sales and growing 16.2% on a daily basis. FMI Technology Signings -- 109 weighted devices per day, totaling 6,993 for the quarter compared to 6,458 in the prior year period. FMI Sales Mix -- 44.6% of total sales, an increase of approximately 60 basis points versus the second quarter of 2025. Heavy Manufacturing Daily Sales -- growing 18.1% year over year, representing the largest end market segment at 44.1% of total sales. Non-Residential Construction Daily Sales -- growing 17.0% year over year, marking the fifth growth period in 15 consecutive quarters. Contract Sales -- growing 17.6% on a daily basis, representing 75.8% of total revenue. Non-Contract Sales -- growing 7.3% on a daily basis, accounting for 24.2% of total revenue. Customer Site Growth -- 16.5% increase in sites spending $50,000 or more per month, with revenues from these high-volume sites growing 26% year over year. SG&A Expenses -- 23.5% of net sales, an 80 basis-point improvement year over year driven by labor productivity and fixed cost leverage. Operating Cash Flow -- $265.7 million, representing 69.4% of net income, down from 84.4% in the prior year due to higher accounts receivable balances. Accounts Receivable -- $1.5574 billion, an increase of 17.6% year over year reflecting strong sales growth in June 2026. Inventories -- $1.7352 billion, a 0.5% increase year over year reflecting disciplined inventory management and optimization. Full-Year CapEx Guidance -- $310 million to $330 million, compared to $230.6 million in 2025, with investments focused on hub capacity, distribution automation, and IT infrastructure. Shareholder Returns -- $305.1 million returned in the quarter through $275.4 million in dividends and $29.7 million in share repurchases. Headcount -- 22,230 full-time equivalent employees, an increase of 1.9% year over year to support sales growth and supply chain throughput. Direct Fasteners and Hardware Daily Sales -- growing 16.8% year over year, slightly outpacing indirect materials growth. Product Pricing Impact -- 2.9% increase in net sales, or 4.5% on a stack basis, as the company lapped the onset of prior year pricing actions. Interest Income -- $1.5 million, down from $2.7 million in the prior year quarter due to slightly lower cash investments. Tunnicliff noted that the "negative 40 basis-points [net price/cost position] that we still sit with today... is going to be 3 or 4 percentage points on the incremental," identifying it as a primary obstacle to achieving mid-20% incremental margins. Tunnicliff identified inflationary pressure in the supply chain, stating that "fuel is 1 of those that we are actually given the amount of volatility... it is still a headwind." SUMMARY Fastenal Company ( FAST -0.03% ) management reported that second quarter results were driven by market share gains among larger customers and a stable industrial environment. The company noted that growth was broad-based across geographic regions and end markets, with particular strength in heavy manufacturing and construction. While gross margins faced headwinds from pricing and customer mix, leadership emphasized that these larger accounts are accretive to operating income through increased volume and operational efficiencies. Digital adoption continues to be a primary focus, with increased sales through FMI and e-business platforms. On the call, management detailed a leadership transition and confirmed that the three-pillar strategy of sales effectiveness, service enhancement, and market expansion remains the core focus for the business. CEO Florness noted that while the company missed its 24% incremental margin target due to gross margin trends, the team "changed the trend" and achieved sequential gross margin improvement. Management reported that the 2026 digital footprint target was adjusted to 63% to 64%, down from 66%, because non-digital sales are growing at a pace that affects the total percentage mix. CFO Tunnicliff stated, "Our pricing actions helped offset the ongoing impacts of tariffs and other inflation," while noting the company continues to chip away at a 40 basis-point net price/cost headwind. President Watts indicated that June sales growth of 20.5% was partly driven by one-off orders and faster business implementation times enabled by new internal quoting and implementation tools. CEO Florness highlighted the efficiency of the workforce, stating, "We spent about $1.6 billion a year in people cost," and emphasized using AI tools to increase group productivity by 5% to 10%. The company is increasing its focus on international markets, with Watts suggesting that acquisitions could accelerate the build-out of global supply chains from 10 years to 2 to 3 years. Management implemented a $0.26 interim dividend per share, aiming for a total annual payout of $1.00 per share to maintain a consistent yield for shareholders. INDUSTRY GLOSSARY FMI Technology : Fastenal Managed Inventory, including vending devices (FASTVend), infrared bins (FASTBin), and scanned stocking locations (FASTStock). DSR (Daily Sales Rate) : Total net sales for a period divided by the number of business days in that period. MEU (Machine Equivalent Unit) : A standardized measure used to quantify the signings and installations of different types of vending and bin devices based on expected output. PMI (Purchasing Managers' Index) : An economic indicator derived from monthly surveys of private sector companies, with levels above 50 indicating expansion. Digital Footprint : A combined metric of sales through FMI technology and e-business tools like electronic data interchange (EDI) and transactional websites. Tunnicliff: Thank you, Jeffery, and good morning, everyone. As in the past, I will review 3 areas with you this morning. The business trends we saw in the quarter the key drivers of margin performance, and how those results translate into cash flow and capital allocation. Overall, the quarter showed continued progress against our strategy. Improving demand trends, solid execution across the business, and strong cash generation. Even with continued uncertainty in the broader economy. I will start on the business trends and market drivers slide. During the second quarter, the industrial environment remained stable and modestly positive. Consistent with the trend we saw in the first quarter. This lines up with the gradual improvement that started late last year. Our daily sales growth improved to 14.7% for the quarter up from 12.4% in the first quarter. Reflecting continued market outperformance. Growth was supported by new customer wins, increased share of wallet with existing customers, pricing, and improved industrial production. Importantly, the improvement was not concentrated in any 1 area. It showed up across customer types and markets. As a result, activity levels remained healthy and our teams continue to see strong customer engagement. From an end market perspective, this slide shows the breadth of that improvement. The common thread across the strongest areas was larger customer engagement and project related activity. Which continues to support our key account strategy. In that environment, our diverse customer base key account focus, and strategic initiatives helped us convert market stability into stronger growth and continued share gains. While these customers typically carry lower gross margins, they generate attractive incremental profit dollars and we remain accretive to operating margin. The higher volumes associated with these relationships drive fixed cost leverage improve asset utilization, and create operating efficiencies across our network. As a result, although the mix shift can moderate gross margin percentage, It supports our broader objective of growing absolute profitability and expanding operating margins over time. That leverage more than offset the gross margin headwinds, and drove margin consistency year over year. Even with continued investment in tech analytics, and sales support. Reflecting strong sales growth good cost control and disciplined capital allocation. In total, our P&L performance shows that we can invest for growth, while staying focused on profitability even as our mix strategically shifts. Toward larger and more complex accounts. Our second quarter conversion rate was driven specifically by higher accounts receivable. Primarily driven by our strong June sales improvement of 20% year-over-year. Year-over-year. Meaning that we go through periods of different investment run rates. 2026 is a year in which we will invest a little bit toward the higher end of that investment range. Reflecting our confidence in cash generation and our commitment to returning value to shareholders. Our capital allocation approach remains unchanged. We prioritize investing in the business where we see strong returns. Returning excess cash to shareholders, and maintaining a conservatively capitalized balance sheet.
